Status.F1: Installed pg-pool reattaches idleListener during release(true); it can re-emit a native client error on the pool and internally remove/end twice. An owned client listener alone is insufficient. This delta handles that pool dispatch route.

minimal_delta.placement: Inside the same private factory module, add one weak per-pool owned-error dispatch gate used only by the proposed adminRetiredSession. Install it before opt-in acquisition; do not alter EventEmitter.prototype, pg-pool internals, a global process handler or other pools.
minimal_delta.gate_contract: Keep the pool original emit function. Its single replacement checks receiver===that exact private pool, event===error and WeakSet.has(second error-event argument). Only when all hold does it mark the exact active owned lifecycle with a fixed error boolean and return true WITHOUT forwarding native error/remaining arguments to pool error listeners or errorMonitor. Otherwise Reflect.apply(originalEmit, receiver, original arguments) exactly preserves Node return/throw/listener behavior. The native error object is not inspected, stringified, stored or re-emitted.
minimal_delta.why_not_listener: An ordinary pool error listener cannot stop other listeners or errorMonitor from seeing the raw owned error. A blanket listener also changes unhandled foreign-error behavior. The narrow dispatch gate avoids both; its intentional effect is limited to the explicitly registered opted-in client.
minimal_delta.identity: Register each exact successfully acquired PoolClient in a WeakSet synchronously inside pool.connect callback, before exposing its query port or invoking owner work. Use a separate WeakMap for that client active lifecycle state. Do not classify by error.client/getters, SQL backend PID, role, URL, message or client properties. Unknown/foreign/missing clients always delegate.
minimal_delta.client_sink: Attach one nonthrowing error sink to each registered owned client before its callback. It only looks up this emitter in the active WeakMap and sets a finite boolean; it retains no native error or raw values. Keep this minimal sink for that client lifetime, including after release invocation throws or active cleanup finishes. A client-owned listener does not itself root the client from the factory.
minimal_delta.lifetime: Keep the same pool gate for that pool object lifetime; do not restore emit/remove ownership when an operation returns because the driver can emit late. WeakSet ownership is not deleted while the client is alive. Delete active WeakMap entries at lifecycle finalization; detach its end/drain/timer/promise observers after the bounded join as applicable. No global strong Map/Set of clients, callbacks or unresolved promises is introduced. The remaining sink/WeakSet do not root retired clients. Pending driver-owned promise rejections remain observed; no SQL/query port remains open.
minimal_delta.installation_integrity: One gate per private pool; subsequent concurrent opt-in sessions share its weak identity routing and maintain separate active state. Do not stack wrappers. Before opt-in work, unexpected replacement of that gate is a fixed capability refusal, not a silent rewrap or private-field fallback. Default code has no access to the private pool; its existing configuration/log remains unchanged.
minimal_delta.concurrency: One owned client error marks only that client active lifecycle; it cannot erase another active registration or suppress foreign-client errors. Registration and active cleanup are per-client; no temporary global listener removal/replacement windows.
minimal_delta.retirement: Catch synchronous exceptions from exactly one public client.release(true) invocation and convert them into fixed retirement failure/UNKNOWN. Do not retry release/end. Installed pool may internally call remove/end more than once after its idle listener error path; do not call that a second public release or promise exactly one driver end. All event-based owned errors before finalization make the lifecycle fail closed. No raw retirement exception escapes the owned API.
minimal_delta.late_events: An owned error after a retirement timeout is still contained by weak ownership and can never promote UNKNOWN. An error after observed closed/settled retirement is also contained without restarting work or retroactively asserting anything about backend rollback/canonical restoration. Finite completion cannot prove absence of all future synthetic events; it proves only recorded query/protocol/end facts. No late event is allowed to emit raw data or reopen the closed query port.

semantic_effects.owned_only: The private pool emit method identity changes when the gate is installed. Raw error/errorMonitor dispatch for registered opted-in clients is intentionally replaced by closed lifecycle facts, including when other pool error listeners exist. This is an explicit new opt-in containment effect, not claimed unchanged behavior.
semantic_effects.foreign_default: For every other event/error/client/receiver the exact original emit is called with unchanged this/arguments. No listener is added to the pool error event, removed or reordered. Zero-listener foreign error still throws its original object; existing foreign handlers and their own throws/return semantics remain intact. Existing default adminSession/adminQuery/adminExec callers are not migrated or certified safe.
semantic_effects.driver_log: Current getPool passes no log option; installed Pool default log is a no-op. No new raw logging is added. The installed idle listener retains its own internal no-op additional-error callback; the factory does not depend on that callback to contain the first pool emission.
semantic_effects.unchanged: Original proposal query/drain and admission bounds, always-retire path, late-acquisition refusal, C1-C7 authority/publication/ordinary callback/restoration/custody, all six candidate paths, all applied migration immutability and zero native/runtime authority remain unchanged.
semantic_effects.future_runtime: No additional query, principal, connection or SQL privilege effect beyond the prior candidate. The only additional runtime behavior is exact opted-in client error dispatch containment and catching retirement invocation failure. Source implementation still requires separate six-path allocation after independent F1 challenge.

precise_gate_pseudocode: owned: WeakSet<PoolClient>; active: WeakMap<PoolClient, finiteOwnedState>; originalEmit = pool.emit
const state = active.get(args[1]); if (state) state.poolError = true;
function ownedClientErrorSink() { const state = active.get(this); if (state) state.clientError = true; }
In exact acquire callback: owned.add(client); active.set(client,state); client.on("error", ownedClientErrorSink);
After closed admission: try exactly-once client.release(true); catch => fixed retirement failure; bounded actual joins/end.
Finalization: active.delete(client); keep weak ownership and minimal client sink; never restore the pool gate.
